flawed_step: The claim ignores the necessary edge-count condition: a self-complementary graph on n vertices requires n(n-1)/4 to be an integer.
counterexample: Take n=6. Any simple graph G on 6 vertices has m edges, while its complement has 15-m edges. If G were isomorphic to its complement, they would have equal edge counts, so m=15-m and hence m=7.5, impossible. Thus no self-complementary graph exists on 6 vertices.
assessment_summary: The universal statement is false because n=6 satisfies n>=4 but admits no self-complementary graph.
